Hi Olivia — really glad the demo was helpful. Short answer: yes, we support safe downgrade paths and have a recommended approach for pilots. I pulled together a quick summary and a pricing matrix (attached) to get the conversation going.

High-level options (preview):
- Core: basic hosted API (generation + embeddings), best for proof-of-concept.
- Pro: Core + dedicated inference pools, higher throughput, long-term KV cache retention.
- Enterprise: Pro + private deployment, SSO/KMS, advanced retention controls and SLA.

Downgrade principles:
- Pro -> Core: possible with a 30–45 day notice; we offer prorated credits for committed capacity and a 90-day KV cache grace period so running workloads don’t fail instantly.
- Enterprise -> Pro: requires migration planning (network config, KMS handoff); we recommend a canary reduction and short-term overlapping capacity to avoid service disruption.

I attached: initial-pricing-matrix.xlsx with sample seat counts and estimated credits for downgrades, and a one-page plan comparison PDF. If you want, I can loop in Laura (account) and Marissa (solutions) to give a firm credit policy and a short SOW draft for procurement.

Hi Olivia / team — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers and a suggested, procurement-friendly approach: 

1) Credit formula: standard approach we use for pilots — 30-day lookback on committed capacity. When a customer downgrades mid-billing period we compute the difference between committed spend and actual usage over the prior 30 days and issue a one-time credit equal to that difference, applied to the next invoice. Example: $40k/mo commit, after lookback the usage-equivalent is $25k -> credit = prorated difference ($15k pro-rated to billing cycle). We can include exact sample math in the SOW.

2) KV cache: we provide a 90-day retention grace period on Pro-tier caches when moving to Core. During the 90 days we do not charge for the cache storage as part of the grace (intended to avoid sudden failures in pipelines). After 90 days the cache is archived and a restore incurs standard restore fees. If the customer keeps Pro capacity while they rehydrate, there's no interruption. Marissa — please flag if that needs any nuance.

3) API stability: Redwood guarantees stable external REST endpoints across tiers (no breaking path changes). Performance SLAs and throughput tokens differ but the API contract remains the same. We will flag any feature-deprecation windows 60 days in advance in the contract.

Attachments: SOW-draft.docx (one‑page SOW + termination/credit language), redwood-plan-comparison.pdf (one‑pager we use for procurement).

Operational recommendation for the pilot: keep a 10% overlap buffer on Pro capacity during the final month of the pilot to absorb traffic spikes; include a one-time migration support credit (we can offer a $3k migration credit for first-year sign-ups).

Happy to join the 11:00 AM PST call to walk procurement through the SOW.
